key_insight: Standardizing prostate cancer EHR data to OMOP and adding NLP plus PSA-based algorithms substantially improved completeness and research usability.
clinical_relevance: This approach can turn routine clinical records into higher-quality prostate cancer datasets for outcomes research, while also helping validate and refine cancer registry data.
method: Converted UTMB Epic EHR data (2010–2021) into OMOP CDM v5.4
Compared OMOP data quality against the Galveston Cancer Registry using agreement metrics
Used NLP and PSA-based rules to extract missing Gleason score, stage, treatment, and biochemical recurrence signals
evidence_signal: Of 815 analytic cases, 700 (85.9%) were complete and concordant with the cancer registry, PSA agreement was excellent, and NLP/PSA algorithms improved capture of sparse clinical fields.
watch_item: The approach depends on local EHR text quality and algorithm tuning, so performance may not generalize without site-specific validation.
paper_title: Developing an OMOP-Standardized Prostate Cancer Database and Improving Data Quality Using NLP and PSA-Based Algorithms
